summary: mask_secret's MIN_MASKABLE_LENGTH boundary (8) lets an 8-character API key leak 7 of its 8 characters into logs and exported QA debug bundles.
failure_scenario: mask_secret('abcd1234') returns 'abc***1234' — only the 4th character is hidden. DebugManager.export_bundle embeds masked_config_dict output in the QA zip the user is encouraged to share; for short tokens (8-10 chars, common for local/proxy gateways) the bundle effectively discloses the secret (1 unknown char = 62 guesses). The contract requires keys be 'masked in any log/export'; this boundary defeats that for short keys. No test asserts a minimum number of hidden characters.
suggested_fix: Guarantee a minimum masked proportion: e.g. require len(value) >= MASK_PREFIX_CHARS + MASK_SUFFIX_CHARS + 4 before partial reveal (return '***' otherwise), or always mask all but the last 4 characters. Add a boundary test for lengths 8-11 asserting at least half the secret is hidden.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced the exact failure: mask_secret('abcd1234') == 'abc***1234' (MIN_MASKABLE_LENGTH=8 at nlapt/core/config.py:31 means the shortest partial-reveal secret shows 7 of 8 chars, leaving 1 unknown char ≈ 62 guesses). Confirmed propagation: DebugManager.export_bundle (nlapt/diagnostics/debug_manager.py:128) embeds masked_config_dict output in the shareable QA zip. This conflicts with the module contract that keys MUST be masked in any log/export and README's 'API key never enters logs' guarantee — for 8-10 char keys the mask is effectively no mask. Test-gap claim also verified: tests/core/test_core_config.py:174 asserts the leaky boundary output ('abcdefgh' -> 'abc***efgh') and no test enforces a minimum hidden proportion. Behavior is intentional/documented (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:186), which justifies low severity but does not refute the security consequence.

summary: restore() creates the pre-restore snapshot before reading the target zip, and create()'s retention pruning can delete the very snapshot being restored, permanently destroying the backup and failing the restore.
failure_scenario: Dataset at the retention cap (e.g. retention=3 with 3 snapshots). User restores (or oplog-rollbacks to) the OLDEST snapshot. restore() calls self.create(PRE_RESTORE_OPERATION), which brings the count to retention+1 and _enforce_retention() unlinks the oldest zip -- the one being restored. The subsequent zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path) raises FileNotFoundError -> SnapshotError 'restore ... failed: [Errno 2] No such file or directory'. Proven by .nlapt-review-scratch/poc_restore_retention.py: restore fails, the target backup zip is gone forever, and a useless pre_restore zip is left behind. Since NLaptApp uses config default snapshot_retention=20 and every batch op plus every restore creates a snapshot, any rollback to the 20th-oldest operation both fails and silently deletes that backup.
suggested_fix: In restore(), read all needed entry bytes from the target zip (or copy the zip aside) BEFORE calling self.create(PRE_RESTORE_OPERATION); alternatively exclude the restore-target path from _enforce_retention pruning for the duration of the restore.
verdict_reasoning: CONFIRMED by direct execution. In nlapt/storage/snapshots.py, restore() (line 143) calls self.create(PRE_RESTORE_OPERATION) before reopening the target zip (line 145), and create() ends with _enforce_retention() (line 104), which unlinks the oldest snapshot when the count exceeds retention. PoC (.nlapt-review-scratch/poc_verify.py): with retention=3 and 3 snapshots, restoring the oldest snapshot produced exactly the claimed outcome — the pre-restore snapshot pushed the count to 4, _enforce_retention() deleted the restore target ('retention pruned old snapshot ...op1.zip'), and zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path) then raised FileNotFoundError, surfaced as SnapshotError 'restore from ...op1.zip failed: [Errno 2] No such file or directory'. After the failed restore: the target backup zip is permanently gone, the caption file still contains the modified (un-restored) content, and a useless pre_restore zip remains. The severity claim also checks out: nlapt/core/config.py:68 sets snapshot_retention=20 as the default and nlapt/app.py:125 passes it to SnapshotManager, so any restore/rollback targeting the oldest retained snapshot at the cap both fails and destroys that backup. Note the entry names are read via _read_entries before create(), but the entry BYTES are read after, which is precisely the window the finding identifies; the suggested fix (read bytes or copy the zip aside before creating the pre-restore snapshot, or exclude the target from pruning) is sound.

summary: A corrupt .nlapt/checkpoints.json makes open_dataset() raise StorageError from the CheckpointStore constructor, rendering the whole dataset unopenable — while a corrupt session.json in the same directory is handled gracefully.
failure_scenario: Reproduced: write '{ this is not json' to <root>/.nlapt/checkpoints.json (disk glitch, external edit, partial copy of the .nlapt dir) -> NLaptApp().open_dataset(root) raises StorageError('checkpoint file ... unreadable or corrupt (delete it to start fresh)') because CheckpointStore.__init__ eagerly calls _load() (checkpoint.py:79) and app.py:127 has no guard. Contrast: a corrupt session.json is caught in _restore_session (app.py:533-536, 'corruption never blocks opening'). A user-facing app would simply fail to open the folder; the actionable 'delete it' hint never reaches the user. No test covers a corrupt checkpoint file at open_dataset time.
suggested_fix: Treat a corrupt checkpoint file like a corrupt session file: catch StorageError around CheckpointStore construction in open_dataset, log + record_error, and fall back to an empty store (optionally renaming the bad file aside). Add a test mirroring the corrupt-session test for checkpoints.json.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced exactly as claimed. Test setup: a minimal dataset (a.png + a.txt) with '{ this is not json' written to <root>/.nlapt/checkpoints.json -> NLaptApp().open_dataset(root) raises StorageError('checkpoint file ... is unreadable or corrupt (delete it to start fresh): Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes...') and the dataset cannot be opened. Control run with a corrupt session.json instead: open_dataset succeeds, logging 'session restore skipped (corrupt file)' — confirming the asymmetry. Code path verified: nlapt/app.py:127 constructs CheckpointStore(result.root) with no guard; CheckpointStore.__init__ (nlapt/batch/checkpoint.py:79, note: batch/checkpoint.py, not checkpoint.py as cited) eagerly calls _load(), which raises StorageError on any malformed JSON (checkpoint.py:131-155). The contrast handler exists at app.py:528-536 (_restore_session catches SessionError, records it via DebugManager, and continues), and open_dataset's own docstring states corruption 'never blocks opening the dataset' — but that promise only covers the session file. Counterargument considered and rejected as insufficient to refute: raising StorageError IS the tested, documented contract of CheckpointStore._load (tests/batch/test_batch_checkpoint.py:136), so the store itself behaves as designed. But neither NLapt.md nor docs/ARCHITECTURE.md requires open_dataset to fail on a corrupt checkpoint file, and checkpoints are strictly less critical than the session (losing them only forces a batch re-run), so the app-level gap — the whole dataset becoming unopenable over an auxiliary resume cache while the analogous session corruption is deliberately tolerated — is a genuine robustness/error-handling inconsistency, and grep confirms no test covers a corrupt checkpoints.json at open_dataset time. Severity medium is appropriate: real user-facing failure with a trivial trigger, but with an actionable message and workaround (delete the file), and only reachable via external corruption since writes are atomic.

summary: _strip_matching_quotes strips the first and last characters whenever they form a quote pair, even when they belong to two different quoted phrases, corrupting valid captions asymmetrically.
failure_scenario: LLM returns the caption '"cinematic lighting" and "bokeh"'. clean_llm_output sees text[0]=='"' and text[-1]=='"' and strips both, producing 'cinematic lighting" and "bokeh' -- unbalanced quotes injected into the caption body, which is then stored as a pending suggestion / translation shown to the user and saved to the txt on accept. Proven by .nlapt-review-scratch/poc_quotes.py.
suggested_fix: Only strip the outer quote pair when it actually wraps the whole string: verify the opening quote's matching closer is the final character (e.g. no unescaped occurrence of the closing quote before the end, or count/scan for balance) before removing.
verdict_reasoning: Confirmed by execution: clean_llm_output('"cinematic lighting" and "bokeh"') returns 'cinematic lighting" and "bokeh' (PoC at .nlapt-review-scratch/poc_quotes.py). _strip_matching_quotes only compares (text[0], text[-1]) against QUOTE_PAIRS and never checks that the opening quote actually closes at the end of the string, so two independent quoted phrases lose one quote each, injecting unbalanced quotes into the caption body. This contradicts the code's own contract comment at line 21 ("stripped when they wrap the whole text") and the spec 7.4 intent of stripping wrapper quotes, and silently corrupts caption data that flows to suggestions/saved txt files.

summary: Two images with the same stem (cat.jpg + cat.png) are both paired with the single cat.txt, creating two independent CaptionRecords aliasing one file; edits through one key silently clobber edits made through the other.
failure_scenario: Dataset contains cat.jpg, cat.png and cat.txt ('original caption'). open_dataset loads both keys with the same txt_path. User edits key 'cat.jpg' to 'edited via jpg key' and saves -> cat.txt updated, but the 'cat.png' record still holds 'original caption'. User later edits key 'cat.png' (starting from the stale text) and saves -> the jpg edit is silently overwritten and lost. Proven by .nlapt-review-scratch/poc_shared_txt.py. Additionally NLaptApp._txt_to_key maps 'cat.txt' to only the last image (line 144 of nlapt/app.py, last-write-wins), so after rollback_operation the reload refreshes only one of the two records, leaving the other permanently stale in the store and search index.
suggested_fix: Detect stem collisions during _scan_directory: when a txt is already claimed by another image, either surface the conflict (ValidationError/warning + orphan-style report) or make all same-stem image keys share one caption record; in NLaptApp, make _txt_to_key map a txt key to ALL image keys and reload every alias after restore.
verdict_reasoning: Confirmed by executing the exact failure scenario (.nlapt-review-scratch\poc_shared_txt_verify.py). With cat.jpg + cat.png + cat.txt in one directory, _scan_directory (nlapt/storage/scanner.py:96-121) groups txts by lowercased stem and pairs EVERY same-stem image with the same txt via _choose_txt (line 110), producing two ImageFile records both with txt_path=cat.txt, no orphan, no warning. open_dataset then loads two independent CaptionRecords aliasing one file. Observed output: after edit('cat.jpg', 'edited via jpg key')+save, disk holds the jpg edit but the cat.png record still holds 'original caption'; a subsequent edit+save through 'cat.png' writes 'original caption tweak' to cat.txt — the jpg-key edit is silently destroyed, exactly as claimed. Also verified app._txt_to_key == {'cat.txt': 'cat.png'} (nlapt/app.py:144, last-write-wins in the open_dataset loop), so _reload_from_disk after rollback_operation would refresh only the cat.png record, leaving cat.jpg stale in the store/index. The spec (NLapt.md 2.1, ARCHITECTURE.md scanner section) defines same-dir/same-stem pairing but says nothing about stem collisions, so this is not spec-mandated behavior; it is silent user-data loss with no surfaced conflict, violating the stated error-handling standard (never silently swallow errors). Finding stands.

summary: accept_for_edit() (and accept_suggestion) rely on set_text's state transition, so with revert_confirmed_on_edit=False the unreviewed AI text lands with state CONFIRMED, violating the contract 'pending becomes DRAFT body text ... NOT confirmed'.
failure_scenario: AppConfig(revert_confirmed_on_edit=False); a caption is CONFIRMED; an AI rewrite attaches a pending suggestion; user clicks '编辑后接受' (accept_for_edit) intending to edit before confirming. state_after_edit keeps CONFIRMED because revert_confirmed=False, so the record returns state=CONFIRMED -- the machine-generated, never-reviewed text is now marked human-confirmed, and next_unconfirmed() skips the file during review. Proven by .nlapt-review-scratch/poc_accept_for_edit.py (prints CaptionState.CONFIRMED; ARCHITECTURE.md line 747 requires DRAFT).
suggested_fix: In accept_for_edit (and arguably accept_suggestion), explicitly force the resulting state to DRAFT regardless of the revert_confirmed_on_edit setting, e.g. add a CaptionStore method that sets text with an explicit target state, instead of reusing the manual-edit transition.
verdict_reasoning: CONFIRMED by executing the failure scenario against the real code (.nlapt-review-scratch/verify_accept_for_edit.py). With CaptionStore(revert_confirmed_on_edit=False), a CONFIRMED caption given a pending suggestion returns state=CONFIRMED from accept_for_edit(): the AI text becomes the body while remaining marked human-confirmed. With the default revert_confirmed_on_edit=True the same call yields DRAFT, proving the state depends on an unrelated config flag. The mechanism is exactly as claimed: nlapt/workflow/suggestions.py:49 delegates to store.set_text(), whose transition (nlapt/core/states.py:47-48) keeps CONFIRMED when revert_confirmed is False; clear_pending never touches state. The scenario is reachable: NLaptApp.set_suggestion (nlapt/app.py:333) and the rewrite batch worker (app.py:406) attach pending suggestions with no state filter, so CONFIRMED captions can carry suggestions. The contract is unambiguous and stated three times: NLapt.md spec 10 line 233 ("编辑后接受（建议载入编辑器成为正文草稿...由用户修改后自行确认）"), docs/ARCHITECTURE.md nlapt.workflow section ("pending becomes DRAFT body text, pending cleared, NOT confirmed"), and the module's own docstring ("it is NOT confirmed"). None of them conditions accept_for_edit's DRAFT outcome on revert_confirmed_on_edit — that flag is a spec-4.1 rule about manual edits of confirmed captions, not about loading unreviewed AI text. Consequence verified in concept: next_unconfirmed skips CONFIRMED entries, so the never-reviewed AI text escapes the review loop. One caveat: the finding's parenthetical about accept_suggestion is weaker — ARCHITECTURE.md explicitly specs accept as "pending -> set_text(...)" with normal transitions, so keeping CONFIRMED there is arguably spec-compliant; the finding itself hedges with "arguably". The core accept_for_edit violation stands. Medium severity is appropriate (silent state corruption in a review workflow under a non-default but supported config).

summary: When a file has a UTF-8 BOM but a non-UTF-8 body, the BOM bytes are not stripped before retrying the candidate encodings, so gb18030/big5/shift_jis fail on the BOM and detection falls through to latin-1 mojibake.
failure_scenario: cap.txt contains b'\xef\xbb\xbf' + '一只猫，坐在窗台上'.encode('gb18030') (a GBK caption a Windows tool prefixed with a BOM). read_text_detect: utf-8-sig fails (body invalid UTF-8), then the loop decodes data INCLUDING the BOM -- gb18030 raises on the BOM byte sequence, and latin-1 'succeeds', returning encoding='latin-1' with text 'ï»¿Ò»Ö»Ã¨...' instead of the Chinese caption. Because needs_conversion=True, the convert-and-resave flow (spec 2.2) then writes the mojibake back as UTF-8, permanently corrupting the caption. Proven by .nlapt-review-scratch/poc_bom_gbk.py (prints encoding: latin-1).
suggested_fix: When a BOM is present but the utf-8-sig decode fails, strip the 3 BOM bytes and run the candidate loop over the remaining body (still flagging needs_conversion=True), so the body is detected as gb18030 correctly.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced the exact failure: a file with b'\xef\xbb\xbf' + gb18030-encoded Chinese body makes read_text_detect return encoding='latin-1' with mojibake text ('ï»¿...') and needs_conversion=True, while the body alone decodes correctly as gb18030. Code path confirmed in nlapt/storage/text_io.py lines 59-84: on utf-8-sig failure the candidate loop decodes the raw data including the BOM, so gb18030 raises (BOM bytes break multibyte alignment) and latin-1, which never fails, wins. Spec NLapt.md 2.2 mandates auto-detection of GBK-family encodings and convert-to-UTF-8 on confirmation, so needs_conversion=True on the mojibake result leads the convert flow to rewrite garbage as UTF-8, permanently corrupting the caption. Suggested fix (strip BOM bytes before retrying candidates) is sound.

summary: Configured LLM retries and rate-limiting (RequestControl.max_retries / min_interval) are dead config, never applied anywhere in the pipeline.
failure_scenario: A user sets request.max_retries=3 and request.min_interval=1.0 in AppConfig to survive a flaky endpoint and avoid 429s. run_rewrite_batch (app.py:413) and Translator.translate (translate.py:160) call client.complete() directly; no code anywhere imports or invokes with_retry / MinIntervalLimiter (grep across nlapt/ shows the only references are in retry.py and __init__.py exports). A single transient LLMRequestError on one item therefore fails that item immediately with zero retries, and concurrent workers fire with no minimum spacing, producing exactly the rate-limit failures the config was meant to prevent. The resilience utilities the contract specifies are wired to nothing.
suggested_fix: Wrap each client.complete() call in the rewrite/translate paths with with_retry(RetryPolicy(max_retries=config.request.max_retries,...)) and gate request starts through a shared MinIntervalLimiter(config.request.min_interval), or drop the fields if genuinely out of scope.
verdict_reasoning: Confirmed. Grep across nlapt/ shows config.request.max_retries and min_interval are never read outside nlapt/core/config.py, and with_retry/MinIntervalLimiter/RetryPolicy are referenced only in retry.py, llm/__init__.py, and tests — no production call site. RewriteService.run_one (nlapt/llm/rewrite.py:183) and Translator.translate (nlapt/llm/translate.py:160) call client.complete() directly with no retry or rate-limiting hook, and the app.py:413 batch path threads only config.request.concurrency (app.py:417). Runtime reproduction with the project's MockLLMClient(fail_times=1) confirms the exact failure scenario: with RequestControl(max_retries=3, min_interval=1.0) configured, both the rewrite and translate paths fail after exactly 1 call on a single transient LLMRequestError — zero retries. The spec unambiguously requires this behavior (NLapt.md:211: 失败重试次数, 默认 2 次, 指数退避; 请求最小间隔) and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md defines RequestControl and the nlapt.llm.retry module for spec 8, so this is a real contract violation: the resilience utilities exist and are tested but are wired to nothing. The only refutation avenue (wiring is the caller's responsibility) fails because the library's own facade consumes the config yet applies only concurrency, and the service constructors offer no retry injection point.

summary: Rewrite-batch checkpoints are persisted to disk while the produced suggestions live only in memory, so a crash silently drops suggestions that resume then skips.
failure_scenario: run_rewrite_batch runs at concurrency 4 and, per successful item, the engine calls checkpoints.mark() which atomically writes .nlapt/checkpoints.json (engine.py:203). The suggestion itself is only stored via self._store.set_pending (app.py:406) and is persisted to session.json solely by save_session(), which the facade calls only from close(). If the process crashes mid-batch (or the user force-quits), the on-disk checkpoint records those keys as done but the in-memory pending suggestions are lost with no session save. On restart the user re-runs the same rewrite to 'resume'; the engine skips every checkpointed key, so those files get no suggestion, are absent from BatchReport.results, and the run reports success — permanent silent loss of completed LLM work.
suggested_fix: Persist each suggestion (or a resumable record of it) at the moment the checkpoint is marked, e.g. save the session/pending atomically alongside checkpoints.mark, or only checkpoint after the suggestion is durably stored.
verdict_reasoning: CONFIRMED by execution. I reproduced the exact failure scenario in a scratch dataset (nlapt\app.py:406, nlapt\batch\engine.py:203-204, nlapt\batch\checkpoint.py:97-107): (1) A rewrite batch interrupted after one success left .nlapt/checkpoints.json on disk containing ['a.png'], while the produced suggestion existed only in the in-memory CaptionStore (set_pending). (2) Simulating a crash (no close()/save_session()), .nlapt/session.json was never written — verified absent. save_session() is called from exactly one place in the library: NLaptApp.close() (app.py:157); nothing in run_rewrite_batch or the engine persists suggestions. (3) On a fresh NLaptApp, open_dataset restored zero pending suggestions, and re-running the identical RewriteSpec produced the same checkpoint_id (make_checkpoint_id is deliberately stable), so the engine skipped a.png. The run finished status=COMPLETED, succeeded=2, failed=0, a.png absent from report.results and with pending=None, and the checkpoint was then cleared — permanent, silent loss of the completed LLM work with no error or warning surfaced to the caller. This is also an unambiguous spec violation: NLapt.md line 261 requires that after abnormal exit, unreviewed pending suggestions are recoverable via the session file, and line 223 promises crash-safe checkpoint resume for LLM batches; as implemented the two mechanisms are inconsistent (checkpoints durable per-item, suggestions durable only on clean close). Even a UI doing periodic save_session() calls (as one test comments) cannot close the window, because checkpoint marks are persisted immediately and atomically per item with no synchronization or reconciliation against restored session state on resume. Severity medium is fair: it silently discards paid LLM output and requires the user to notice missing suggestions and run a third pass. Suggested fix direction (persist suggestions alongside/before checkpoint marks, or reconcile checkpoints against restored pending on resume) is sound.

summary: skip_if_present uses raw str.startswith/endswith, so a trigger word is silently NOT added whenever the caption merely begins with the trigger as a substring of a longer word.
failure_scenario: Reproduced: make_trigger_add_op('cat').apply('caterpillar on a leaf') returns 'caterpillar on a leaf' unchanged — the trigger 'cat' is never added because 'caterpillar'.startswith('cat') is True; likewise PrefixSuffixSpec(suffix='cat') skips 'a bobcat'. In a batch trigger-add over a LoRA dataset (spec 7.2's core use case), every caption whose first token happens to extend the trigger string silently loses its trigger word, and the BatchItemResult reports ok with 'no change' — the training set ends up with missing trigger words and no error. Existing tests (test_ops_prefix_suffix.py:56-75) only cover exact-match presence, never the substring boundary.
suggested_fix: Check presence against a boundary, not a raw prefix: skip only when text == prefix or text.startswith(prefix + joiner) (and for non-empty joiners also consider the canonical ', '), or compare against split_chips(text) for chip-style captions. Add tests: trigger 'cat' must be added to 'caterpillar ...' and suffix 'cat' to '... bobcat'.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced exactly as claimed: make_trigger_add_op('cat').apply('caterpillar on a leaf') returns the input unchanged, and suffix='cat' skips 'a bobcat' — nlapt/ops/prefix_suffix.py:82,93 use raw str.startswith/endswith without any boundary or joiner awareness. This contradicts the option's documented purpose in both the spec (NLapt.md 7.2 line 175: skip exists to '防止触发词被重复叠加' — prevent double-stacking of trigger words) and the module's own docstring ('prevents trigger words from being stacked twice'): when the caption merely starts with a longer word extending the trigger, nothing would be duplicated, yet the trigger is silently never added. The removal path is deliberately exact-match including the joiner (spec line 177; remove_exact_prefix), making the raw-substring add-skip inconsistent with its own contract. The silent-success claim is also confirmed: nlapt/app.py:298 emits BatchItemResult(ok=True, detail='no change') for unchanged items, so a batch trigger-add over a LoRA dataset would report success while captions lack their trigger word. Existing tests (tests/ops/test_ops_prefix_suffix.py:56-75) only cover exact-presence, never the substring boundary. The only defense is a hyper-literal reading of 'begins with the prefix' in the spec sentence, which is contradicted by that sentence's own rationale clause; the failure mode (silent training-data corruption in the feature's core use case) is real.

summary: RequestControl.timeout, max_retries, and min_interval are dead config: the entire retry module (with_retry, MinIntervalLimiter, RetryPolicy) has zero call sites, and RewriteService/Translator build LLMRequest without a timeout, so the hardcoded 60s default always applies.
failure_scenario: Grep-verified: only config.request.concurrency is ever read (app.py:417); nothing in nlapt/ imports with_retry or MinIntervalLimiter outside retry.py itself, and rewrite.py:176-182 / translate.py:153-159 construct LLMRequest with no timeout argument. Concrete: a user configures AppConfig(request=RequestControl(timeout=300, max_retries=3, min_interval=1.0)) for a slow local Ollama model; every rewrite/translate request still aborts with LLMTimeoutError at 60s, a transient HTTP 429/500 immediately fails the batch item with zero retries, and concurrency-4 requests are fired with no pacing — all three documented, tested config knobs (spec 8 / RequestControl contract: 'max_retries: exponential backoff') are silently ignored. The retry module has 98% unit-test coverage yet is never integrated, which coverage numbers cannot reveal.
suggested_fix: Wire RequestControl through the request path: pass timeout=profile/request timeout into LLMRequest in RewriteService.run_one and Translator.translate, wrap client.complete calls in with_retry(RetryPolicy(max_retries=config.request.max_retries)), and share one MinIntervalLimiter across batch workers. Add an integration test asserting a configured timeout/max_retries actually reaches the client and that a transiently failing MockLLMClient (fail_times=1) succeeds after retry.
verdict_reasoning: CONFIRMED by both static analysis and runtime execution. (1) Grep over nlapt/ shows with_retry, RetryPolicy, and MinIntervalLimiter are referenced only in nlapt/llm/retry.py itself, the nlapt/llm/__init__.py re-exports, tests, and docs — zero production call sites. (2) Of RequestControl's four fields, only concurrency is ever read (nlapt/app.py:417); timeout, max_retries, and min_interval are read nowhere outside config construction/serialization in nlapt/core/config.py. (3) nlapt/llm/rewrite.py:176-182 and nlapt/llm/translate.py:153-159 build LLMRequest without a timeout argument, so DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 60.0 (nlapt/llm/base.py:34,96) always applies; RewriteService.__init__ accepts only text_client/vision_client/profile/trigger — there is no parameter through which RequestControl could even reach the request path. (4) Runtime test executed: with a spy client, RewriteService.run_one produced request.timeout == 60.0 regardless of any RequestControl(timeout=300); and MockLLMClient(fail_times=1) caused run_one to raise LLMRequestError immediately with zero retries, despite the spec (NLapt.md line 211) explicitly requiring configurable timeout, min request interval, and retry count 'default 2, exponential backoff' (指数退避), and RequestControl's own docstring/comment promising the same. This is an unambiguous spec/contract violation, not a style preference: three documented, serialized, unit-tested config knobs are silently ignored end-to-end.

summary: When two images share a stem (a.jpg + a.png both pairing with a.txt), the _txt_to_key map is last-wins, so after rollback_operation one image's in-memory record keeps the rolled-back (stale) text with dirty=False — re-saving it silently undoes the rollback.
failure_scenario: Reproduced: dataset with a.jpg, a.png, a.txt('original'). apply_operation replacing 'original'->'changed' writes a.txt; rollback_operation restores disk to 'original', but _reload_from_disk resolves txt key 'a.txt' to only a.png (app.py:144 overwrote the a.jpg mapping), leaving app.caption('a.jpg').text == 'changed' while disk and a.png say 'original', with dirty_keys() == (). If the user then edits/confirms a.jpg starting from the stale 'changed' text, save() writes it back and the rollback is silently reverted. Also, the batch processed the same physical txt twice (double-apply hazard for non-idempotent ops like prefix add with skip disabled).
suggested_fix: Make _txt_to_key map txt keys to a list/tuple of image keys (or detect shared-stem groups at scan time) and reload every image record sharing the restored txt in _reload_from_disk; alternatively deduplicate keys by txt_path in apply_operation. Add a scanner+facade test with two images sharing one stem covering batch apply and rollback.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced end-to-end with a runnable script (.nlapt-review-scratch/repro_shared_stem.py). The scanner (nlapt/storage/scanner.py:132-139) deliberately pairs multiple same-stem images (a.jpg, a.png) with one a.txt, so the shared-stem setup is a supported dataset shape, not an artificial input. app.py:144 populates _txt_to_key with last-wins semantics, yielding {'a.txt': 'a.png'}. After apply_operation('original'->'changed') and rollback_operation, observed state was exactly the claimed failure: disk='original', a.png record='original', a.jpg record='changed' with dirty_keys()==() (stale text, clean flag). A subsequent save('a.jpg') wrote 'changed' back to disk, silently reverting the rollback. This violates the facade's own documented contract ("After rollback_operation the affected captions are reloaded from disk"). The secondary double-apply hazard is also confirmed: the oplog record's affected_keys was ('a.txt','a.txt') and the batch wrote the same physical txt twice. Severity medium is appropriate: requires a shared-stem dataset, but the consequence is silent data corruption of a rollback.

summary: Resumed AI rewrite batches silently skip checkpointed keys whose pending suggestions were lost in the crash, then report COMPLETED — the suggestions are unrecoverable and no error is surfaced.
failure_scenario: Reproduced: run_rewrite_batch over 4 files is interrupted after all items were dispatched (checkpoint marks all 4 keys on disk via CheckpointStore.mark, but pending suggestions live only in the in-memory CaptionStore and session.json is only written by close()/save_session()). Process dies without close(). New NLaptApp.open_dataset() restores zero pendings; re-running the identical rewrite computes the same checkpoint_id, the engine skips all 4 keys, produces 0 results, reports BatchStatus.COMPLETED, and clears the checkpoint. Observable: pending_keys() == (), report says COMPLETED — the user paid for 4 LLM calls and got nothing, with no indication anything is missing. Root cause: checkpoint durability (disk) is decoupled from result durability (memory); tests/app/test_app_integration.py:199 masks this by calling save_session() before simulating the crash, and no test exercises checkpoint resume through the facade.
suggested_fix: Make checkpoint marking and result persistence atomic from the engine's perspective: in run_rewrite_batch, save the session (or at least persist the new pending suggestion) before/when the engine marks the checkpoint — e.g. call save_session() in the worker after set_pending, or subscribe to EVT_BATCH_PROGRESS/FINISHED to save the session. Add an integration test: interrupt a rewrite batch, reopen without close(), re-run, and assert every key ends up with a pending suggestion.
verdict_reasoning: CONFIRMED by execution. Repro script (.nlapt-review-scratch\repro_checkpoint_loss.py) simulated a process death mid-run_rewrite_batch after all 3 items were checkpoint-marked (KeyboardInterrupt escaping the engine, app dropped without close()). Observed on-disk state after crash: .nlapt/checkpoints.json contained all 3 keys, session.json did not exist. A fresh NLaptApp.open_dataset() restored 0 pending suggestions; re-running the identical rewrite (same checkpoint_id from make_checkpoint_id(operation, keys, repr(spec))) produced: status=completed, 0 results, 0 new LLM calls, 0 pending suggestions, and the checkpoint file was cleared to {} — the 3 paid LLM results are permanently unrecoverable with no error, no failed items, and no indication anything is missing. Mechanism verified in source: CheckpointStore.mark persists to disk synchronously after every success (nlapt/batch/engine.py:203-204, checkpoint.py:97-107), while the results (PendingSuggestion set at nlapt/app.py:406-409) live only in the in-memory CaptionStore and are persisted solely by save_session()/close() (app.py:153-161, 441-465). The engine clears the checkpoint on COMPLETED (engine.py:130-131), destroying even the evidence of the lost run. This is not a style issue: NLapt.md spec 9 explicitly promises crash-safe resume ("任务中断（含程序崩溃）后再次发起相同操作时提示'从断点继续'") and the test class TestSessionCrashRecovery docstring claims "drafts + pending suggestions survive a crash" — but tests/app/test_app_integration.py:199 calls save_session() before the simulated crash, masking the gap, and no test exercises checkpoint resume through the facade. The counter-argument that a UI is expected to call save_session() periodically does not refute the finding: nothing in the core does so, and even periodic saves leave a structural window (per-item synchronous checkpoint marks vs. periodic session saves) in which marked-but-unsaved suggestions are silently lost on resume. Severity high is justified: silent loss of paid LLM work reported as COMPLETED.

summary: SnapshotManager.restore() creates the pre-restore snapshot (which enforces retention) before extracting the target zip, so restoring the oldest snapshot at retention capacity permanently deletes the very backup being restored and the restore then fails.
failure_scenario: Verified by repro: dataset with retention=N and N snapshots in .backups/ (default 20 per spec 2.4); user restores the oldest snapshot. restore() first calls self.create(PRE_RESTORE_OPERATION), pushing the count to N+1; _enforce_retention() deletes the oldest zip, which is the restore target; the subsequent zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path) raises FileNotFoundError -> SnapshotError('restore ... failed: No such file or directory'). The chosen backup is gone forever and the caption files are NOT restored, breaking spec 2.4's guarantee that restore is safe and the snapshot system is the final safety net. Even restoring a non-oldest snapshot at capacity silently destroys the oldest backup as a side effect of the restore.
suggested_fix: In restore(), exclude the restore-target zip from retention pruning (or read all selected entry bytes into memory / keep the archive open before calling create()), e.g. pass an `exclude` path down to _enforce_retention, or defer retention enforcement until after extraction succeeds.
verdict_reasoning: Confirmed by direct repro against the actual code (nlapt\storage\snapshots.py). In restore() (line 143), self.create(PRE_RESTORE_OPERATION) runs before the target zip is reopened for extraction (line 145), and create() calls _enforce_retention() (line 104), which deletes the oldest zips beyond the retention limit with no exclusion for the restore target. Repro executed: with retention=3 and 3 snapshots, restoring the oldest snapshot raised SnapshotError('restore from ...op0.zip failed: [Errno 2] No such file or directory'), the target zip was verified deleted from disk (exists: False), and the caption file was NOT restored (still contained the modified content). The pre-restore snapshot pushed the count to N+1, retention pruned the oldest zip — which was the restore target — and the subsequent zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path) hit FileNotFoundError. This is not a style issue: the spec (NLapt.md line 52) requires the snapshot system to guarantee rollback safety ('恢复动作本身也生成一份恢复前快照，保证可以反悔'), and here the chosen backup is permanently destroyed while nothing is restored. The corollary in the finding is also correct: even restoring a newer snapshot at capacity silently deletes the oldest backup as a side effect. Severity 'high' is justified — irreversible data loss in the component whose entire purpose is being the final safety net.

summary: Spec 8 request controls are never applied on any real LLM request path: RewriteService.run_one and Translator.translate call client.complete() directly with no retry (spec default: 2 retries with exponential backoff), no MinIntervalLimiter, and without propagating the configured RequestControl.timeout (LLMRequest always carries the 60s default).
failure_scenario: Verified by repro: MockLLMClient(fail_times=1) makes run_one raise LLMRequestError after exactly 1 call — a single transient network/429 error during a batch puts the file on the failed list even though spec 8 mandates 2 retries with exponential backoff by default. Likewise a user who sets request.timeout=300 for a slow local Ollama model still gets requests issued with timeout=60.0 (captured request.timeout == 60.0 in both rewrite and translate paths), causing spurious LLMTimeoutError. with_retry and MinIntervalLimiter in nlapt/llm/retry.py are exported but referenced nowhere in the pipeline (grep-confirmed); RequestControl.min_interval and max_retries are dead config. Same defect in nlapt/llm/translate.py:160.
suggested_fix: Thread RequestControl into the request path: build LLMRequest with timeout=config.request.timeout, wrap client.complete in with_retry(RetryPolicy(max_retries=config.request.max_retries)), and share a MinIntervalLimiter across batch workers (call limiter.wait() before each request). RewriteService/Translator could accept a RequestControl (or retry policy + limiter) at construction, wired by NLaptApp.run_rewrite_batch.
verdict_reasoning: Confirmed by execution and code inspection. (1) Repro ran: MockLLMClient(fail_times=1) makes RewriteService.run_one raise LLMRequestError after a single attempt — no retry, though NLapt.md spec 8 (line 211) mandates default 2 retries with exponential backoff (失败重试次数默认 2 次，指数退避). (2) Repro captured the request built at nlapt/llm/rewrite.py:176-183: timeout == 60.0 (LLMRequest dataclass default), because RewriteService never passes timeout= and nothing in the codebase reads config.request.timeout; nlapt/llm/translate.py:153-160 has the identical pattern. (3) Grep confirms with_retry/MinIntervalLimiter exist only in retry.py, __init__ exports, tests, and docs — referenced by no request path — and of RequestControl only concurrency is consumed (app.py:417); min_interval/timeout/max_retries are parsed in config.py and never read. This is a concrete, reproducible spec/contract violation (silently ignored user config, single transient error fails a batch item), not a style preference.

summary: skip_if_present tests raw text.startswith(prefix) / endswith(suffix) instead of an exact prefix+joiner (or whole-chip) match, so the operation silently skips files whose caption merely begins with a longer tag sharing the prefix string — leaving files without their trigger word.
failure_scenario: Verified by repro: batch-add trigger 'minahamu' (spec 7.2 trigger preset, skip_if_present default on) to caption 'minahamuko, 1girl, solo' -> unchanged; add trigger 'girl' to 'girls dancing in the rain, blue sky' -> unchanged; add suffix 'masterpiece' to '1girl, this piece is a masterpiece' -> unchanged. Each item reports ok/'no change', so files end up missing the trigger word with no failure signal, defeating the option's stated purpose (preventing duplicate stacking without skipping files where the trigger is actually absent). Note the asymmetry: remove_exact_prefix requires the exact 'prefix+joiner' text, while the add-skip fires on any shared leading substring.
suggested_fix: Skip only on an exact match: text == prefix or text.startswith(prefix + joiner) (and for arbitrary joiners, additionally treat the comma-joiner case as a whole-chip check via split_chips); mirror the same rule for the suffix.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced all three claimed scenarios by executing the actual code: make_trigger_add_op('minahamu').apply('minahamuko, 1girl, solo') returns the text unchanged, make_trigger_add_op('girl') on 'girls dancing...' unchanged, and suffix 'masterpiece' on '...this piece is a masterpiece' unchanged; preview() returns () so batch runs report no change with no failure signal. Line 82 uses raw text.startswith(spec.prefix) (line 93 endswith), while remove_exact_prefix requires exact prefix+joiner — the asymmetry is real. Caveat: NLapt.md 7.2's literal mechanism wording ('已以该前缀开头时跳过') describes startswith, but the same sentence and the module docstring state the option's purpose is preventing duplicate stacking of trigger words; here the skip fires when the trigger is absent, silently leaving files without their trigger word, so the demonstrated behavior defeats the documented intent. Low severity is appropriate.

summary: While paused, the engine blocks in controller.wait_if_paused() inside the dispatch loop and never collects already-finished in-flight futures, so EVT_BATCH_PROGRESS, on_progress callbacks, and checkpoint marks for completed items stall until resume.
failure_scenario: LLM rewrite batch with concurrency>=2: k1 (slow) and k2 dispatched; user pauses; k1's worker finishes (API call paid, pending suggestion set). The engine is blocked at wait_if_paused before collecting k1, so no progress event fires and CheckpointStore.mark('...','k1') is not persisted. If the process crashes or is killed while paused (the exact situation pauses are used for), the resume run re-executes k1, paying for the LLM call again. Proven by .nlapt-review-scratch/poc_pause_blocks_collect.py: progress for the finished k1 arrives only after resume().
suggested_fix: Restructure _execute so pausing stops only new dispatches: e.g. wait on futures with a timeout and drain completed ones each iteration, or check controller state without blocking while in_flight is non-empty and only block in wait_if_paused when in_flight is empty.
verdict_reasoning: Confirmed by running a live PoC against the actual code (BatchEngine.run with concurrency=2, keys [k1 slow, k2 fast, k3 pending], a real BatchController, and take_snapshot=False). Sequence observed: after pause, k2 was still collected (engine was inside _wait_futures at that moment), then the engine looped back to the dispatch phase — with k3 pending and a free slot it blocked in controller.wait_if_paused() at nlapt/batch/engine.py:186. When k1's worker then finished while still paused, NO progress callback fired for k1 for 1.5s of waiting; k1's progress arrived only after controller.resume() (PoC output: 'k1 progress fired while paused: False', 'k1 progress fired only after resume: True'). Since CheckpointStore.mark (line 203-204) and EVT_BATCH_PROGRESS (line 205-208) execute in the same collection block that stalls, the checkpoint mark for the completed-and-paid item is also not persisted until resume — so a kill-while-paused would re-execute that item on resume, exactly the claimed failure. Caveats: (1) the stall only occurs when there are more keys than concurrency (with exactly `concurrency` keys, next_key is None and the engine waits in _wait_futures, collecting normally) — but that is the normal batch case and matches the finding's scenario; (2) the code comment 'pause blocks right here' and progress.py's docstring show pausing-at-dispatch is intentional, and no spec text promises progress delivery during pause, so this is a durability/observability defect rather than an unambiguous spec violation — 'low' severity is appropriate. The cited PoC filename in the finding does not exist in the scratch dir, but my independent reproduction validates the behavior.

summary: run_rewrite_batch persists checkpoint marks durably but stores the produced suggestions only in memory, so a crash before the session is saved makes the resume run silently skip keys whose suggestions were lost.
failure_scenario: User runs an AI rewrite batch over 100 keys and cancels at 60 (checkpoint keeps 60 marks in .nlapt/checkpoints.json by design). The app crashes before close()/save_session() writes .nlapt/session.json, so the 60 in-memory pending suggestions are gone. On reopen, re-running the identical batch computes the same checkpoint_id, skips the 60 'completed' keys, processes the remaining 40, completes, and clears the checkpoint -- the run reports success while 60 files never received a suggestion and the report contains no trace of them.
suggested_fix: Couple the two durability domains: save the session (which persists pending suggestions) after a rewrite batch finishes or is cancelled, and/or on open_dataset drop checkpoint entries whose keys have no corresponding pending suggestion in the restored session before resuming.
verdict_reasoning: Empirically confirmed by running the exact scenario (scratch script .nlapt-review-scratch\repro_v2.py). Mechanism verified in code: (1) the worker in run_rewrite_batch (nlapt/app.py:406) stores results only via self._store.set_pending — in-memory CaptionStore state; (2) BatchEngine._execute marks the checkpoint durably to .nlapt/checkpoints.json after EVERY successful item (nlapt/batch/engine.py:203-204, CheckpointStore.mark persists atomically per mark, checkpoint.py:97-107); (3) pending suggestions are only persisted by save_session(), which the library calls solely from close() (app.py:157) — no event subscriber or post-batch hook saves the session (only the wildcard DebugManager logger subscribes internally); (4) open_dataset/_restore_session does not reconcile checkpoints against restored pending suggestions. Repro output: after a cancelled run with 4 succeeded items and a simulated crash (app dropped without close(), session.json never written), checkpoints.json retained all 4 marks; on reopen no pending was restored; re-running the identical batch (same checkpoint_id) skipped all 4 keys, returned status=COMPLETED, succeeded=0, failed=0, empty results, and cleared the checkpoint — the suggestions are permanently lost with zero trace in the report. This also contradicts the checkpoint module's own crash-recovery contract (checkpoint.py docstring: resume 'after an interruption (including a crash)' skips completed keys — but after a crash those keys are not actually completed, since their only output vanished) and NLapt.md line 223's crash-resume promise. Severity 'low' is fair (window requires a crash before close, and the suggestions are re-derivable at LLM cost), but the finding is real, not a style preference.

summary: open_dataset discards TextReadResult.needs_conversion (and encoding), so the spec 2.2 flow — detect non-UTF-8, prompt, convert-and-resave on confirmation — cannot be implemented on top of the core facade; legacy-encoded txt files stay in their original encoding on disk indefinitely.
failure_scenario: A dataset contains GBK-encoded caption txts. open_dataset decodes them via read_text_detect but keeps only .text; no event is published, no API exposes which keys need conversion, and DatasetScanResult carries nothing about encoding. A (future) UI therefore cannot offer the spec 2.2 conversion prompt, and unless the user happens to edit and save each individual file, the txts remain GBK on disk forever — despite spec 2.2 requiring unified UTF-8 (no BOM) storage with a detect-and-convert-on-confirm workflow. grep confirms needs_conversion is produced in storage/text_io.py and consumed nowhere.
suggested_fix: Collect keys whose TextReadResult.needs_conversion is True during open_dataset and surface them (e.g. a keys_needing_conversion() facade method or a published event plus a convert_to_utf8(keys) method that rewrites via write_caption), so the prompt-and-convert flow of spec 2.2 is drivable through the core.
verdict_reasoning: Empirically confirmed, not just by inspection. Repro (scratch dataset with a GBK-encoded caption txt): open_dataset decoded the text correctly, but (1) zero events were published during open (subscribed to every EVT_* in nlapt/core/events.py), (2) DatasetScanResult carries only root/images/orphan_txts — no encoding data, (3) the NLaptApp facade has no method mentioning encoding/conversion, (4) the record is not dirty after load, so save_all_dirty() saved nothing and close() left the file byte-identical GBK — invalid UTF-8 on disk after a full open/save/close cycle. Grep confirms TextReadResult.needs_conversion (nlapt/storage/text_io.py:39,68,83) is consumed nowhere except its own tests; nlapt/app.py:140 takes `.text` and discards encoding + needs_conversion. The spec violation is unambiguous: NLapt.md section 2.2 (line 44) requires "检测到非 UTF-8 时提示用户并在确认后转换保存" (on detecting non-UTF-8, prompt the user and convert-and-save on confirmation), and text_io.py's own docstring says the flag exists "so the caller can offer a convert-and-resave prompt" — the sole caller drops it. Since the architecture (app.py docstring and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:761) states a future UI binds ONLY to bus events and facade methods, the spec 2.2 prompt-and-convert workflow is unimplementable through the documented core surface; the only workaround (UI re-reading every txt via read_text_detect directly, then calling app.save) bypasses the facade contract and duplicates I/O. One mitigating note: the ARCHITECTURE.md NLaptApp contract itself lists no conversion API, so app.py conforms to the written facade contract — the defect is a product-spec gap in the core surface, which supports the medium (not high) severity. Finding is real as stated.

summary: AI rewrite batches are logged to the operation log with snapshot=None, so the spec-required whole-operation rollback (spec 9: '全部批量操作写入操作日志并可整体回滚'; spec 7.5 batch entries provide 整体回滚) raises OperationError, and there is no core-level bulk way to undo the batch's pending suggestions.
failure_scenario: Verified by repro: run_rewrite_batch over 3 files appends an oplog record 'AI rewrite:polish · 3/3 files' with snapshot=None; calling app.rollback_operation(record.op_id) raises OperationError('no snapshot was taken for it') and all pending suggestions remain attached. A user who ran a bad prompt over the whole dataset (the spec's own example entry 'AI 重写（视觉）· 产生待审核 32 条') cannot roll the operation back through the history log as spec 7.5/9 require; they must reject every suggestion one key at a time.
suggested_fix: Give rollback a non-snapshot path for suggestion-producing operations: e.g. record the affected caption keys with kind='ai_batch' and have rollback_operation clear_pending() on those keys (appending a rollback record), or add a facade-level reject_all(keys)/bulk-reject tied to the oplog entry.
verdict_reasoning: Repro confirmed end-to-end: run_rewrite_batch over 3 files (nlapt/app.py:413-428, take_snapshot=False at line 420) appends an oplog record 'AI rewrite:polish · 3/3 files' with snapshot=None and kind=BATCH_KIND; app.rollback_operation(op_id) then raises OperationError('cannot roll back operation #1 ... no snapshot was taken for it') via nlapt/history/oplog.py:115-119, and all pending suggestions remain attached. The spec is unambiguous: NLapt.md section 9 lists 'AI 操作' among batch capabilities that all go through '自动快照' and states '全部批量操作写入操作日志并可整体回滚'; section 7.5 says '批量类条目提供整体回滚' and gives 'AI 重写（视觉）· 产生待审核 32 条' as its own example of a batch log entry. The implementation records the AI batch as a batch-kind entry yet denies rollback. Refutation attempts failed: the docstring's 'no disk snapshot needed' rationale does not satisfy the rollback contract (rollback neither succeeds nor clears the pending suggestions it would need to undo); docs/ARCHITECTURE.md documents only the created-keys rollback limitation, not this one; and grep confirms no core-level bulk reject/accept (only per-key reject_suggestion), so the spec's whole-operation undo has no core substitute. Medium severity is fair since data is not corrupted and per-key reject still works.

summary: run_rewrite_batch persists checkpoint marks per item (checkpoints.json) but never persists the produced pending suggestions (session.json is only written by close()/save_session()), so after a crash or cancel+crash the resume run skips keys whose suggestions were lost, and those files silently never get a suggestion.
failure_scenario: Verified by repro: run an AI rewrite batch over 4 files, cancel (or crash) after 2 items, then the process dies without close(). checkpoints.json durably records img0/img1 as completed, but their PendingSuggestions existed only in the CaptionStore. On restart, open_dataset finds no session pending state; re-running the identical rewrite (same checkpoint id) skips img0/img1 per spec 9 断点续跑 — final pending keys are only img2/img3, and img0/img1 permanently never receive a suggestion. This contradicts spec 12 ('程序异常退出后重启可恢复...未处理的待审核建议') combined with spec 9's resume semantics: checkpoint durability outpaces result durability.
suggested_fix: Make suggestion persistence at least as durable as the checkpoint: call save_session() inside the worker after set_pending (or from EVT_BATCH_PROGRESS / at batch end including CANCELLED status), or only mark the checkpoint after the pending suggestion has been persisted to the session file.
verdict_reasoning: Confirmed by executable repro (no source modified). CheckpointStore.mark persists checkpoints.json atomically after every successful item (checkpoint.py:97-107, called from engine.py:203-204), while the pending suggestions produced by run_rewrite_batch's worker exist only in the in-memory CaptionStore (app.py:406-409); session.json is written solely by close()/save_session() (app.py:153-157, 441) and nothing invokes save_session during a batch. Repro: 4-file dataset, rewrite batch cancelled after 2 items, process 'crashes' without close() -> checkpoints.json records img0/img1, session.json absent. On restart, open_dataset restores no pending; re-running the identical rewrite skips img0/img1 (same checkpoint id), completes img2/img3, and clears the checkpoint -> img0/img1 permanently and silently never receive a suggestion. This violates NLapt.md line 261 ('程序异常退出后重启可恢复未落盘的草稿与未处理的待审核建议') combined with line 223's checkpoint-resume semantics: checkpoint durability strictly outpaces result durability. The 'UI does periodic save_session' defense only narrows the window; the core never orders suggestion persistence before the checkpoint mark, so the loss window is inherent. Severity high is justified: silent permanent loss of paid LLM batch results with no detection path after the checkpoint is cleared.
